{{nihongo|'''Nagara Shrine'''|長柄神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Yamato Province]].

It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}}; its former rank under the {{ill|Q712534|lt=old ranking}} was {{ill|Son-sha|Q134917284|qid=Q134917284}}. It is also called "Hime-no-Miya."

=== Enshrined deity ===
The shrine enshrines one deity<ref name="説明板">Precinct information board.</ref>:
* {{ill|Shitateruhime|Q11307233|qid=Q11307233|lt=Shitateruhime-no-Mikoto}} (したてるひめのみこと)

Texts also present other theories: {{ill|Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|lt=Kotoshironushi|Q8009611|qid=Q8009611|qid=Q8009611|lt=Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto}} or Takateruhime-no-Mikoto{{Sfn|長柄神社（式内社）|1982年}}. The Kotoshironushi theory derives from '{{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|Q1045362|qid=Q1045362}}' entry "Yamato Province divine lineage, Nagara no Obito" which states the ancestor as "Ame-no-yae Kotoshironushi." The Takateruhime theory derives from {{ill|Katsuragi Mitoshi Shrine|Q11620955|qid=Q11620955}} (also popularly called "Nagarahime Shrine") enshrining Takateruhime as associated deity{{Sfn|長柄神社（式内社）|1982年}}. Another view says the Nagara clan originally enshrined their ancestor deity, but later traditions linking this shrine as a "hime-no-miya" of {{ill|Katsuragi Hitokotonushi Shrine|Q11620885|qid=Q11620885}} or {{ill|Takakamo Shrine|Q11673295|qid=Q11673295}} gave rise to Takateruhime (sister deity of Kotoshironushi) and Shitateruhime (sister deity of {{ill|Ajisukitakahikone|Q506610|qid=Q506610|lt=Ajisukitakahikone-no-Mikoto}}) theories{{Sfn|長柄神社（神々）|1985年}}.

=== History ===
Founding is unknown{{Sfn|長柄神社（式内社）|1982年}}. The '{{ill|Kojiki|Q813031|qid=Q813031}}' mentions "Katsuragi Nagae"; "Nagae" and "Nagara" are said to be synonymous, meaning a long ridge of Mount Katsuragi<ref name="説明板"/>. There is also a theory identifying this place with "Hegumi Nagara Oka-saki" in the '{{ill|Nihon Shoki|Q813935|qid=Q813935}}' pre-enthronement chronicle of {{ill|Emperor Jimmu|Q200188|qid=Q200188}}, year Kimi, 2nd month, 20th day{{Sfn|長柄神社（式内社）|1982年}}{{Sfn|長柄神社（神々）|1985年}} (another theory identifies it with Nagara-chō in {{ill|Tenri, Nara|Q502196|qid=Q502196}} by context). Texts also note that the '{{ill|Nihon Shoki|Q813935|qid=Q813935}}' entry for {{ill|Emperor Tenmu|Q335181|qid=Q335181}} 9 ({{ill|680|Q23453|qid=Q23453}}), 9th month, 9th day says the emperor held mounted archery at "Nagara no Mori," inferred as this shrine grove{{Sfn|長柄神社（式内社）|1982年}}{{Sfn|長柄神社（神々）|1985年}}.

In the '{{ill|Engishiki|Q1342448|qid=Q1342448}}' {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932|lt=Jinmyōchō}} compiled in {{ill|Enchō|Q1327274|qid=Q1327274}} 5 ({{ill|927|Q30470|qid=Q30470}}), it is listed in {{ill|Katsujō district|Q11620858|qid=Q11620858}}, Yamato Province, as "Nagara Shrine, small, hoe and quiver," indicating listing as {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}} and that hoes and quivers were offered by the court at {{ill|Kinensai|Q118906710|qid=Q118906710}}{{Sfn|長柄神社（式内社）|1982年}}.

Later history is unclear, but ridge tags survive back to {{ill|Shōwa (1312–1317)|Q1324807|qid=Q1324807}} 1 ({{ill|1312|Q5734|qid=Q5734}}) of the {{ill|Kamakura period|Q236205|qid=Q236205}} for construction/reconstruction of the honden. Also, a 1418 ({{ill|Ōei|Q1193078|qid=Q1193078}} 25) "Handa-shō Chūshinbun" in the 'Kasuga Shrine documents' records "Nagara no Miya," identified with this shrine{{SFn|長柄神社（平凡社）|1981年}}.

=== Precinct ===
[[File:Nagara-jinja (Gose) honden.JPG|thumb|220px|right|{{center|Honden (Nara Prefecture designated cultural property)}}]]
The honden is ikken-sha {{ill|Kasuga-zukuri|Q3193781|qid=Q3193781}}. Exterior is vermilion-lacquered; the roof was formerly {{ill|cypress bark roof|Q90373477|qid=Q90373477}} but is now copper-plate roofed. Zen-style details are seen; though construction date is unknown, it is estimated to date back to the mid-{{ill|Muromachi period|Q334845|qid=Q334845}}. Seventeen ridge tags survive, oldest from 1312; from style they are inferred to correspond to tags of {{ill|Kakitsu|fa|کاکیتسو|fr|Ère
